headlines.summary: Treasury yields fell for another day. Chip stocks also moved higher, with investors looking ahead to Nvidia's earnings.
headlines.article_text: Stock market today: Live updates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Traders work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) during morning trading on Aug. 24, 2026 in New York City. Angela Weiss | AFP | Getty Images The S&P 500 rose slightly Tuesday, as Treasury yields fell for a second day. A rally in semiconductor stocks lifted the Nasdaq Composite. The broader index gained 0.2%, while the Nasdaq Composite advanced 0.5%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was little changed. Bond yields slid, with the benchmark 10-year Treasury note yield falling to 4.658%. It declined on Monday as well after CNBC reported that the Treasury Department could use its $1 trillion General Account to fund bond repurchases. Chip stocks rallied, ahead of Nvidia 's results due out after the close on Wednesday. Shares of the Jensen Huang-helmed company were up more than 1%. Advanced Micro Devices and Micron Technology added 3% each. Intel advanced more than 2%. Consumer names were a notable laggard, with shares of Dick's Sporting Goods plunging more than 27% following disappointing results. The sports equipment retailer is on pace for its worst day on record. Other retailers such as Walmart and Target were also under pressure, falling 1% and 3%, respectively. Canada on Tuesday announced retaliatory tariffs against the United States, with the government saying it will match the 50% levies that President Donald Trump imposed over the weekend "dollar for dollar." Investors are also awaiting the personal consumption expenditure price index reading for July out on Wednesday, though inflation concerns eased somewhat with oil prices lower this week. On Tuesday, oil prices dropped more than 3% . "Investors are making guesses on earnings and macro analysis that will be coming out," said Sam Stovall, chief investment strategist at CFRA. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh ends the week Friday with a speech at the Fed's annual symposium in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, a potentially market moving catalyst. His speaking engagement comes after the Treasury Department announced a plan to tame long-dated Treasury yields. 12 Min Ago Canada announces retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% against U.S. goods Dominic LeBlanc, Minister of Internal Trade of Canada speaking on CNBC's Squawk Box on Aug. 25th, 2026. CNBC On Tuesday, Canada said it would slap retaliatory tariffs against the United States, applying to roughly $20 billion in goods. The new tariffs, set to take effect on Sept. 8, would apply to more than 700 U.S. goods and range from 15% to 50%. These duties would target steel, aluminum, dairy, seafood and more. Ottawa's new levies come after the U.S. announced additional 50% tariffs on a variety of Canadian products, targeting motor vehicles, alcohol and dairy. Read more from CNBC's Kevin Breuninger on Canada's tariffs here . — Darla Mercado 22 Min Ago 180 S&P 500 advancers Breadth was poor on Tuesday, even with the S&P 500 higher during midday trading. Shortly into the eleven o'clock hour, there were only 180 advancers in the broader index. Of the 11 S&P 500 sectors, four were in positive territory, led by information technology and health care. The worst laggards were consumer staples and energy. — Sarah Min 29 Min Ago JPMorgan positive on SpaceX's AI capabilities Nikolas Kokovlis | Nurphoto | Getty Images JPMorgan analysts are confident on SpaceX' s AI work, noting its "increasingly positive" on Grok in a Tuesday note. They noted SpaceX's acquisition of Cursor this month will help the company strengthen its AI capabilities. "Cursor brings ~$4B of ARR (as of June 2026), with ~75% coming from businesses, which should help streamline SpaceX's go-to-market strategy & provide valuable data for model training," they wrote. They also noted Cursor data on Grok models has improved its performance. Grok 4.6 improved by five points on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index versus the previous Grok 4.5. Grok 4.6 falls behind Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 & Claude Opus 5 in the ranking, the analysts wrote. JPMorgan maintain its overweight rating and set a price target of $240 for December 2027, implying a 77.7% rise from Monday's close. The stock was last higher by 1.5%. — Ananya Chetia 40 Min Ago CoreWeave profit margins are heading up, says Freedom Capital Markets Omar Marques | Lightrocket | Getty Images Profit margins are on the rise at artificial intelligence computing company CoreWeave , according to a Tuesday analysis from Freedom Capital Markets. 2026 adjusted operating margins are expected to increase from 1% in the first quarter and 5% in the second to 7% in the third and 15% in the fourth. The investment bank sees adjusted EBITDA for the company going from 56% up to 69% this year. "Although we may be a bit aggressive here, if we're even close as this plays out, investors will begin to appreciate CRWV's potential earnings power and [cash flow] generation," Paul Meeks, head of tech research at the bank, wrote. In an interview earlier in August, Meeks described the recent margin expansion at CoreWeave and rival Nebius as "very nice" and "well beyond expectations." --Tobias Burns 1 Hour Ago Consumer outlook dims on worries over jobs Consumer confidence edged lower in August and grew particularly downbeat about the look further down the road. The Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index moved to 89.4, down 0.8 points and below the Dow Jones consensus for 90.2. While the headline index decline was offset by a 6.8-point jump in the present situation measure to 121.2, the expectations index, which gauges the six-month outlook, slid to 68.2, down 5.8 points. "Consumer appraisals of current business conditions were mildly positive. Perceptions of the current labor market improved, reversing three months of moderate decline," said Dana Peterson, the board's chief economist. "Looking ahead, consumers were more pessimistic about business conditions and the labor market over the next six months." —Jeff Cox 1 Hour Ago Weaker than expected new home sales July new home sales came in at a seasonally adjusted rate of 607,000, missing the 620,000 consensus estimate from FactSet. It was also below the prior month's revised 678,000. — Sarah Min 2 Hours Ago JPMorgan expects strong performance from Palo Alto Networks Nikolas Kokovlis | Nurphoto | Getty Images JPMorgan expects Palo Alto Networks will deliver strong fourth quarter results ahead of the company's earnings call on Sept. 1. "We see potential for upside to 4Q26 results and the company's FY27 outlook as elevated pipeline traction is not yet fully embedded in company guidance," the analysts wrote. The analysts maintained its overweight rating for the global artificial intelligence and cybersecurity company with a higher price target of $384 for December 2027, implying a 9.4% increase from Monday's close. — Ananya Chetia 2 Hours Ago Stocks open higher Tuesday Stocks opened higher Tuesday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 125 points, or 0.2%.
